question_answered: Can every retained key be joined to helper, browser, and collector windows without changing the benchmark result?
required_inputs: retained-key id; input/EventDispatch timebase; helper pid/policy; renderer pid; collector file placeholders
advance_condition: 100% of retained keys have join fields, and the compact q50 class ordering matches the existing uninstrumented run.
fallback_condition: Do not run root counters yet; fix join fields or observer overhead first.

question_answered: Do frequency, cluster residency, process QoS, AMP counters, or thermal/power state distinguish fast and slow classes?
required_inputs: sidecar join plus no-CPU slow, ordinary/utility fast, background/maintenance slow, fresh finite, and stale finite rows
advance_condition: One sampled OS state predicts ordinary/utility fast rows and finite decay while absent from no-CPU and background/maintenance slow rows.
fallback_condition: If sampling cadence misses key windows or counters do not separate rows, add system trace.

question_answered: If powermetrics is insufficient, do runnable latency, QoS placement, wakeup timing, or processor selection explain the rows?
required_inputs: same compact rows with trace notifications joined to retained keys
advance_condition: Scheduler/QoS timing predicts the same fast/slow split after accounting for frequency and residency.
fallback_condition: If trace overhead changes class ordering or scheduler state still does not separate rows, test browser scheduler state.

question_answered: After OS state is controlled, do browser queue, task priority, V8, or runtime slices explain the residual?
required_inputs: matched browser runtime/scheduler categories plus source spans and OS-counter alignment
advance_condition: Browser queue/task state predicts residual latency when OS frequency/residency/QoS does not.
fallback_condition: If browser trace duplicates the OS split or perturbs the path, keep the mechanism at the OS-counter layer.

question_answered: If OS and browser scheduling are both insufficient, is the remaining split a cache/memory hierarchy effect?
required_inputs: lower-level counters or specialized profiler support joined to retained EventDispatch windows
advance_condition: Renderer stall or miss ratios separate fast and slow rows without matching frequency, QoS, or scheduler differences.
fallback_condition: Do not claim cache/memory from JS timing alone.

question_answered: Is there one named state variable that predicts all discriminating rows?
required_inputs: joined per-key table containing all successful compact rows and observer controls
advance_condition: No-CPU slow, ordinary/utility fast, background/maintenance slow, and finite decay all follow the same recorded state.
fallback_condition: If only medians agree or different row families need unrelated explanations, leave the mechanism unnamed.
